 The Nevada men’s basketball team plays Saint Mary’s on Sunday at the Tahoe Blue Event Center. Nevada Sports Net’s Chris Murray breaks down the game with his three keys to victory and prediction. This feature is presented in partnership with Bradley, Drendel & Jeanney .
 Nevada (1-0) vs. Saint Mary’s (1-0) 
 When: Sunday, 1:30 p.m.
 Where: Tahoe Blue Event Center (5,000 capacity)
 TV/Radio: None/95.5 FM
 Online: None
 Betting line: No line listed yet
 Three keys for Nevada to win 
 1. Defend the three: Saint Mary’s has played two regular-season games this year. In the first, it made 4-of-16 3-pointers. In the second, it made a school-record 20-of-31 3-pointers. Major difference there. But it shows the Gaels’ ceiling from three. Any team that bangs 20 3-pointers is dangerous. Plus, Saint Mary’s made 13 3-pointers in an exhibition game against Utah State. This team can shoot, and Nevada must mark those shooters. The Gaels have had 11 players make at least one three, so it’s a team-wide approach. The most dangerous shooter is Joshua Dent, who is Saint Mary’s top returning player. He’s made 5-of-9 threes and is a career 40.4 percent shooter from distance. Holding the Gaels to single-digit threes is key.
 2. Second-chance points: The Wolf Pack has not been as good of a 3-point shooting team during its exhibition/early regular-season games, but that means more rebounds are available. And Nevada has been snatching those. After grabbing 14 and 12 offensive rebounds in its preseason games, Nevada snared 21 in the regular-season opener against Robert Morris. That was the program’s most since a double-overtime game against Pacific in 2015. Given the Wolf Pack’s athleticism, the offensive glass should be an advantage this season. Obviously Nevada would prefer for the first shot to go down, but second-chance points will be big against a Gaels team that has allowed 11.5 offensive boards per game this season, matching a Wolf Pack strength against a potential Saint Mary’s weakness.
 3. Win with depth: The Wolf Pack was without two rotation players in its season opener – wing Keyon Kensie Jr. and point guard John Mattingly were both out with minor injuries and could return Sunday – but still flexed its depth with 10 players scoring. Saint Mary’s is also deep with 10 Gaels averaging at least 5.5 points per game. So, both teams have excellent benches and areas to sub if the starters are struggling. One of those Saint Mary’s depth pieces is center Jazz Gardner, who began his career at Nevada in 2024-25 before transferring to Saint Mary’s last season when he redshirted. Gardner has started both games for the Gaels this season and is averaging 5.5 points on 55.6 percent shooting.
 Prediction 
 Nevada 77, Saint Mary’s 73: This isn’t your parents’ Saint Mary’s team. Longtime head coach Randy Bennett, who led the Gaels for 25 seasons and to 589 wins, is now at Arizona State. Promoted in his place was associate head coach Mickey McConnell, who starred for the Gaels from 2007-11 and has been on staff since 2019. He has Saint Mary’s playing at a much faster tempo. The early returns have been positive with wins over Illinois State (90-85 in overtime) and North Dakota State (by 41 points). This despite the team losing five of its top-six scorers, although the Gaels have reloaded with transfers from Stanford, Louisville and Cal Baptist plus a top-100 freshman recruit. Nevada must keep Saint Mary’s shooters at bay in what should be a big résumé game come Selection Sunday. Season record: 1-0
